plan.title: The kickoff after a step agreed the night before reminds, with the tip, and checks they're still in (#92)

context.text: [voice note] That was way better than yesterday. I slowed the jogs right down and could actually talk.
That's the whole trick: slow enough to talk. So tomorrow: 2 min jog, 1 min walk, 4 rounds at the park at 7, about 15 minutes. Work for you?

transcript.text: Morning, Riley! Yesterday you slowed the jogs to talking pace and the second round got easy, so that's the move again today. Tonight at 7 at the park: 2 min jog, 1 min walk, 4 rounds, about 15 minutes. Still locked in like you said last night?

runs.saved:
Reflection for 2026-11-01: Slowing the jogs to talking pace made the second round easy
Step set for 2026-11-02, agreed: 2 min jog, 1 min walk, 4 rounds at the park at 7 pm (about 15 min)

checks.reason: Reminds of the agreed step (2 min jog, 1 min walk, 4 rounds at 7) without re-proposing or asking what time, and closes with a question that assumes the yes.
Brings back yesterday's talking-pace lesson in passing as part of the kickoff, not as a quiz.
Three sentences with exactly one question at the end.
Warm and sincere with no emoji or overfamiliarity, though the energy is a bit more measured than full Pushy.

conversation.reason: The kickoff reminds Riley of the agreed step and ends with 'Still locked in like you said last night?', not a first-time 'you in?'. The slow-enough-to-talk tip is only implied by 'talking pace', so it is borderline.

grade.summary: ZOH's single kickoff handled the regression case well: it reminded Riley of the agreed 2-and-1 step at the park at 7, referenced the talking-pace lesson, and asked a light question that assumes the yes. The main weakness is that the tip is implied rather than stated outright, and the energy runs a little calmer than the Pushy default.
